dropped.item: The reassurance that none of this means a plan is wrong for the reader
The reassurance that visitors are welcome to leave the planning chat with nothing more than a clearer idea of their options
The advice to 'think carefully before you sign' is narrowed to reading the small print only

changed.item: 'they aren't right for everyone' became 'Others will be better off without one'. This shifts from a hedged statement that plans don't suit everyone to a firmer claim that some families would be better off with no plan.

The balanced closing caveat (a plan 'deserves a close look at the small print first') became a direct instruction near the opening ('read the small print before you sign'). The tone is more directive and less reassuring.
